Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate — For the Petitioner 
Nazrul Islam for Korban Ali, Advocates — For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Sirajuddin Mondal -----  Petitioner
Vs.
Amena Khatun and others  ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. It appears that the opposite parties filed the Title Suit for a decree for declaration that they are the sole heirs of Yasin Mondal. They also prayed for a further declaration that the order dated 29.9.84 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer, Pangsha in Miscellaneous Case No. XIII-64/83-84 is illegal, null and void, etc. The plaintiffs claimed that they were the sole heirs of Yasin Mondal, son of Jadu Mondal. They also claimed that Bishu Mondal was father of Jadu Mondal and he had no other son except Jadu Mondal. But recently the defendant No. 1 claiming himself to be chachata brother of Yasin Mondal filed a Mutation case and fraudulently obtained an order dated 29.2.84 from the Upazila Revenue Officer allowing mutation in respect of the share claimed by him in the suit property. In fact, the defendant No. 1 Serajuddin Mondal is not a chachata brother of Yasin Mondal and never possessed any property of Yasin Mondal. As he falsely claimed himself to be a chachata brother of Yasin Mondal and as he obtained fraudulently an order of mutation, the plaintiffs filed the suit for getting the relief mentioned above. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations contained in the plaint. He claimed that Shariatullah had two sons named Gopal Mondal and Bishu Mondal, Gopal Mondal died leaving behind two sons in Taju and Baju. Taju died leaving behind two sons in this defendant and his brother Daimuddin. Baju died unmarried and this defendant and his brother Daimuddin inherited the share of Baju Mondal. This defendant further claims that Bishu Mondal died leaving behind two sons in Adu Mondal and Jadu Mondal Adu died leaving behind one son in Ismail and Jadu died leaving behind one son in Yasin and widow Matijan. Ismail died leaving behind two daughters Khudiram and Kiran and chachata brother Yasin Mondal. Yasin died leaving behind 5 daughters in the plaintiffs and chachata brother in this defendant. In this way, this defendant inherited 3 annas 6 gandas 2 karas 2 kranties share in the property left by Yasin and he has been possessing his share of the property and got his name mutated in respect of his share by filing a mutation case before Upazila Revenue Officer. 

 4. Further case of the defendant is that Bahadur Mondal, one of the co-sharers of the suit property, died leaving behind daughter in Putiran Bibi, wife in Sundari Bibi and two sons of two chachata bothers in this defendant and Yasin Mondal respectively Putiran sold her share to this defendant by registered kabala dated 8.4.70. In that kabala it is stated that Yasin Mondal and Serajuddin Mondal were chachata brothers. The defendant also claimed that the plaintiffs in order to deprive his legal share in the suit property filed the present false suit. 

 5. The learned lower Court, on consideration of the evidence on record came to a finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their exclusive possession in the suit property and, as such, the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned lower Court also believed the case of the defendant and found him to be chachata brother of Yasin Mondal. On such findings, the learned lower Court dismissed the suit. Against that judgment and decree, the plaintiffs preferred an appeal before the court of the District Judge, Rajbari. The appeal was numbered as Title Appeal No. 25 of 1988 and was heard and disposed of by the learned District Judge himself. The learned District Judge found that the defendant No. 1 has lineal connection with Yasin Mondal and also found that the plaintiffs acquired 16 annas interest in the suit property including the two annas share of the widow of Yasin Mondal which they acquired by way of gift. The learned appellate Court also found that the determination of the question of possession is redundant because the plaintiffs prayed for declaration of their heirship to the extent of 16 annas in the suit property. After arriving at such finding, the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the lower Court and decreed the suit. 

 8. At the time of hearing, on perusal of the record and the judgments passed by the courts below, it appeared that both the courts were under a misconception that the suit was filed for a decree for declaration of title of the plaintiffs in the suit property. From the prayer portion of the plaint, it appears that the plaintiffs prayed for two declarations-(1) that the plaintiffs are the sole heirs of Yasin Mondal, (ii) that the order dated 22.9.84 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer of Pangsha in Miscellaneous Case No. XIII-64/83-84 is illegal, null and void, etc. It further appears that the plaint was not amended with regard to the prayer originally made by the plaintiffs. So, it is clear that in this suit the plaintiffs did not pray for declaration of their title in the suit property but unfortunately, both the courts below treated it as a suit for declaration of title. The learned trial Court in its judgment observed as follows:-" As it is a case for declaration of plaintiff's title I think it is necessary to adjudicate the possession". After making such observation the court discussed about the evidence on the question of possession and after referring to the statements of the witnesses of both sides, the court came to a conclusion that the plaintiffs failed to prove their exclusive possession in the suit property and after arriving at such a conclusion, the court held that the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Thus, from the above it is quite clear that the learned trial Court treated the suit to be a suit for declaration of title of the plaintiffs in the suit property. The learned appellate Court though considered that the question as to who were the heirs of Yasin Mondal was the pertinent question to be decided, yet the operative portion of the judgment shows that the appellate Court also treated the suit to be a suit for declaration of title. The relevant portion is reproduced here:- " It is declared that the plaintiffs acquired 16 annas share upon the suit property as heirs of Yasin Mondal and also under a deed of gift from defendant No. 3 Halimunnessa." It is interesting to note that the plaintiffs themselves did not make such a prayer for declaration in the plaint. The relevant prayer of the plaintiffs as made at prayer (a5) is as follows: 

 9. It further appears that the plaintiffs have also prayed for a declaration that an order dated 22.9.84 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer in a mutation case is illegal, null and void, etc. The order has not been marked exhibit either by the trial Court or by the appellate Court but curiously enough the appellate Court declared the order as illegal, null and void, etc. without admitting that order into evidence. It is not understood how an order can be declared to be illegal unless the same is before the court. The District Judge declared the order illegal when the order was not admitted into evidence and marked as an exhibit. The learned appellate Court committed an error of law in declaring the order illegal without admitting the order into evidence and marking it an exhibit. 

 10. From the record it further appears that the plaintiffs though prayed for declaring them as sole heirs of Yasin Mondal, they admitted in the plaint itself that the defendant No. 3 was the widow of Yasin Mondal. From the evidence it transpires that the defendant No. 3 Halimunnessa is the second wife of Yasin Mondal. She is obviously an heir of Yasin Mondal. When it is admitted that defendant No. 3 is wife of Yasin Mondal, the question of declaring the plaintiffs as sole heirs of Yasin Mondal does not arise at all. At the time of hearing, when it was pointed out to the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party/ plaintiffs he frankly conceded that the prayer (ক) of the plaint was a wrong prayer. There cannot be any doubt the prayer (ক) is wrong. Even according to the case of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs cannot be considered as sole heirs of Yasin Mondal. So, they cannot get a declaration as prayed for in the plaint at prayer (ক). The learned appellate Court without properly appreciating the prayer declared that the plaintiffs acquired 16 annas share in the suit property as heirs of Yasin Mondal. It appears that the defendant No. 3 gifted her share to the plaintiffs. It is also mentioned in the plaint that the plaintiffs got the share of defendant No. 3 on the basis of a deed of gift dated 13.8.84 but in spite of such gift it cannot be said that the defendant No. 3 is not an heir of Yasin Mondal. The learned Advocate for the opposite party/plaintiff frankly admitted that the frame of the suit was defective and the prayer was also defective and so he prayed for sending back the suit on remand for fresh trial after giving an opportunity to the plaintiffs to make necessary amendments of the plaint. 

 11. From the above, it is clear to me that both the courts below could not appreciate the question of law involved in the suit and the courts disposed of the suit and appeal under some misconception. It further appears that the plaintiffs were also under some misconception as a result of which they made a wrong prayer at prayer (ক). In this suit, the main question is, who the heirs of Yasin Mondal Admittedly are, the plaintiffs are five daughters of Yasin Mondal and defendant No. 3 is widow of Yasin Mondal. The defendant's case is that one Shariatullah died leaving behind two sons Bishu and Gopal. He further claims that Yasin Mondal is a descendant of Bishu Mondal and he is descendant of Gopal Mondal The courts below came to contradictory decision as reads the genealogy given by both sides. As this court found some defects in the frame of the suit and also found that the courts below were under some misconception while deciding the suit and the appeal, it appears to me that at this stage no decision should be given on this disputed question of genealogy by this court. It also appears to me that for ends of justice, the suit should be sent back on remand as prayed for by the learned Advocate for the opposite party/ plaintiff.
